verdict.rationale: Pinecone's security docs say API key permissions can be managed in the console under role-based access control, and they list API keys and service accounts among production security features. That is first-party evidence of scoped credentials, but the pack never shows how granular the scoping is (e.g., read-only or per-index/namespace), how keys are issued programmatically, or any agent-specific least-privilege guidance. missing for 10: documented permission granularity/scope options, programmatic (API/CLI/MCP) key issuance for agents, agent-oriented least-privilege guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can manage API key permissions in the Pinecone console... Pinecone uses role-based access controls (RBAC) to manage access to resources.
Overview of Pinecone security features for production: API keys, SSO, service accounts, audit logs, CMEK encryption, backups, and Private Endpoints.
